title: Nasdaq Rebounds From Correction as Chips Lead; Dow Flat as Strong Jobs Report Lands
dek: Stocks stabilized Friday after Thursday's AI-led rout. Chip shares led the rebound, the Dow was roughly flat, and the 8:30 a.m. ET jobs report beat forecasts.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Black-and-white photograph of an automatic ticker apparatus on the New York Stock Exchange trading floor
image.credit: Library of Congress via Wikimedia Commons

keyPoints: Yahoo Finance's live page, updated 7:46 a.m. PST (10:46 a.m. ET), showed the Dow up 0.1%, the S&P 500 up 1% and the Nasdaq Composite up 1.9% after its Thursday correction (Yahoo Finance).
Chip names led: Nvidia rose 5.9%, Micron 6.8%, AMD 10.2% and Broadcom 4.9% in the day's trading, per Trading Economics' daily summary.
The October jobs report showed payrolls up 165,000 against a Dow Jones forecast of 59,000; unemployment was 4.1% (BLS; CNBC).
Thursday's rout erased $2.3 trillion in market value; the Nasdaq logged its steepest one-day decline in 19 months (Yahoo Finance; Reuters via Yahoo).

Closing numbers: the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.09% to 24,579.42, the S&P 500 rose 0.31% to 7,376.86 and the Dow fell 237.33 points to 51,285.73 (CNBC live updates). See the afternoon close recap: close-recap-nasdaq-rebounds-1-09-percent-dow-falls-237-points-draftkings-plunges.
body:
## Early trade: a bounce after the correction

U.S. stocks steadied on Friday after Thursday's AI-led sell-off. At 10:46 a.m. ET, Yahoo Finance's live page showed the Dow up 0.1%, the S&P 500 up 1% and the Nasdaq Composite up 1.9%. The Nasdaq had slipped into correction territory on Thursday, and the rout had erased $2.3 trillion of market value, Yahoo reported.

The concern behind the sell-off was less about this week's data than about whether a Democratic sweep of Congress would slow data-center construction and AI spending. Chip stocks took the hardest hit and then led the rebound.

## Chips lead the rebound

Trading Economics' daily summary described technology as the top-performing sector and consumer staples as the laggard. It reported Nvidia up 5.9%, Broadcom up 4.9%, Micron Technology up 6.8% and AMD up 10.2%, with Tesla up 1.9%. Dip-buying in the major chipmakers is what paused the sell-off, the summary said.

## The jobs report lands at 8:30 a.m.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000 in October, above the Dow Jones forecast of 59,000 (CNBC), though Business Insider cited a 65,000 consensus, and that the unemployment rate changed little at 4.1%. The BLS also reported average hourly earnings up 0.4% on the month and 3.1% over the year. Professional and business services led with a gain of 70,000, followed by health care at 42,000.

Traders had been pricing a rate increase from the Federal Reserve. CME FedWatch odds for a quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting were 76.8% after the report, according to CNBC.

## What we do not know yet

The picture is intraday. None of the sources reviewed gives a settled close, and the Trading Economics figures are a daily summary rather than a timed quote. Readers should treat the index levels above as a point-in-time snapshot.

marketImpact.summary: The rebound is led by chips, which carry the most direct exposure to the AI-spending worry. The stronger jobs report adds to rate-hike odds, which is a headwind for rate-sensitive stocks even as it steadies sentiment.
marketImpact.timeframe: Friday, Nov. 6, from the 8:30 a.m. ET jobs release through the midday session

tickers.rationale: Nasdaq Composite up 1.9% at 10:46 a.m. ET (Yahoo Finance), after its correction on Thursday.
Up 5.9% in the day's trading (Trading Economics).
Dow was roughly flat, up 0.1% at 10:46 a.m. ET (Yahoo Finance), with the jobs beat weighing against it.

FOMC meeting Dec. 8-9; hike odds at 76.8% (CME FedWatch via CNBC).
